findings.summary: Part (c) duplicates check_code_survey, which runs first; the round-trip-deliverable branch is dead and the AC3 record fixtures would be refused by the wrong check
findings.evidence: Read in surveys.rs:217-230: `check_code_survey` refuses a reading with any `is_record_or_data_deliverable` deliverable unless a `Code survey:` assumption satisfies `names_record_evidence`. It reads only the survey text, never the deliverable list. checks.rs runs `check_code_survey` first, and the new step comes directly after it. So: (1) A reading with a record deliverable and no record evidence in its survey (AC3's 'no accepted record kind and no round-trip test deliverable') is refused by `check_code_survey`, and the corpus case's `Refuse("check_behavior_test_reading")` would mismatch. (2) 'The same reading with a created crates/athena-data/tests/round_trip.rs deliverable is accepted' fails unless the survey also names check_record_file or round_trip, because a round-trip deliverable does not satisfy `check_code_survey`. (3) Whenever a record deliverable reaches the new check, the survey already names record evidence, so the 'round-trip deliverable path' alternative in (c) can never be what satisfies (c). The `SURVEY` fixture (reading.rs:7037-7038) says only 'allow-list was read', which is not record evidence. Fix: State that the (c) contradiction fixtures have a `Code survey:` naming `check_record_file`, so `check_code_survey` passes and the new check is the refuser. The contradiction is then `Record kind: none` against a record deliverable the survey says is accepted. Remove the round-trip-deliverable branch from (c), or state that it applies only after `check_code_survey` has passed. Add a corpus case showing that a record deliverable with no survey evidence is still refused by `check_code_survey`, and say in the plan that this is how AC3's first contradiction is refused.
findings.location: Decision 2 (part c), Step 3, Criterion 3 demonstration item (1), corpus case record-kind-none-with-new-record-file

findings.summary: The directly-before negation refuses ordinary negated lists, against AC3's 'a negated mention is accepted'
findings.evidence: Under the plan's rule, `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `not through skip_probe nor ATHENA_NO_PROBE` and `no skip_probe, no helper stand-in` are each refused for the second item, because no negator is directly before it. These are the natural ways a reader writes the negated mention. Only one false case is pinned (`no probe runs when skip_probe is set`). Fix: Carry a negation across a coordinated list of matches joined by `or`, `nor`, `and` or a comma. Add a corpus case `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE` (Accept) and list the remaining false cases under Limits.

findings.summary: The `criterion N` collector does not match the plan's own `criteria 1-4` fixture form
findings.evidence: Decision 3 requires each non-routine behavior criterion to be 'named `criterion N`', but Step 5's `CLAUSES` writes a `Direct check:` 'naming criteria 1-4'. The plan does not say whether plurals, ranges (`1-4`) or lists (`2 and 3`, `2, 3`) are recognised. Fix: Define the accepted forms: `criterion N`, `criteria N-M`, and `criteria N, M and K`. Add a unit test for each form, and make `CLAUSES` use one that is tested.

findings.summary: A backticked command counts as an identifier, so a 'direct check' that is only a run command satisfies (d)
findings.evidence: 'An identifier is any of: a token with `_` or `::`, a backticked token, ...'. Read as a backtick span, `Direct check: criterion 2: `cargo test -p athena-core`` holds an identifier and passes (d), although it names no function that measures the property. This is the indirect check the request wants refused. Fix: Do not count backticked spans that contain whitespace or start with `cargo`/`athena `. Or require the (d) identifier to be a function-like token (`_`, `::` or `name()`). Add a refusing test for a command-only Direct check.

findings.summary: Adds a third negator list and negation rule instead of reusing an existing one
findings.evidence: `requires_existing_code_section` (surveys.rs:1370) already has `NEGATORS` with a 3-word window, and verify.rs:1261-1380 has `NEGATORS` with clause-level `is_negator`. The plan adds a third list with different members (`instead`, `than`, `avoid`). `than` alone accepts phrases such as `faster than skip_probe`. Fix: Move one shared negator list into surveys.rs for both reading checks, or explain why this check needs a different list. Drop the bare `than`, or require `rather than`.

summary: Round 2 fixes the round-one findings. Part (b) now reuses `Existing code:`. Skip switches come from a closed list, so `skip_note` passes. Flags are stripped before the routine-criterion test. AC4 is measured on real readings by `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294, confirmed: it runs after each parsed report and prints the share and the limit). The unchanged deliverables are excused through `unchanged_planned_files` (run/mod.rs:1621-1637, confirmed). The functions the plan names exist at the cited lines: `check_code_survey`:199, `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`:237, `names_record_evidence`:164, `existing_code_assumptions`:1329 and `names_existing_path`:1341. The dependents list matches the callers I found by Grep: `check_reading_text` is called from steward.rs, drain.rs, main.rs, replay.rs, run/tests.rs and the corpus, and `Code survey:` fixtures appear only in reading.rs, the corpus and the briefs. One design gap remains, and it is major. Part (c) overlaps `check_code_survey`, which runs first. That check already refuses any record or data deliverable unless the `Code survey:` text itself names `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` or a round-trip test (surveys.rs:217-230). So the new rule's round-trip-deliverable branch is dead code. The planned AC3 fixtures also depend on survey text the plan never specifies: as written, the 'none with a new record file' corpus case would be refused by `check_code_survey` rather than by the new check, and the 'accepted with round_trip.rs' case would be refused too. The other findings are minor. The directly-before negation rule refuses common negated lists. The `criterion N` collector does not match the plan's own `criteria 1-4` fixture. A backticked command counts as an identifier, which weakens (d). The plan also adds a third negator list instead of reusing an existing one.
